fix: drop GCRO-DR warm start on a system change and reject a corrupt one (F-010)

GcrodrState.previous_solution was reused whatever system the state came
from. A dimension change panicked in copy_from_slice, which aborts the
process under panic = "abort", and after an operator or preconditioner
change the old solution seeded a different system.

unknown or differs from the one stored in the state, the rule LGMRES
already applies. A warm start whose length differs from the system
dimension can then only come from a corrupt state; it returns
CoreError::Dimension and the snapshot restore leaves the state
untouched. LGMRES gets the same length guard. The recycle basis handling

branches.message:
fix: error-scaled inner forcing budget and no step-0 abort (F-009, F-008, F-031, F-030)

Step B (F-009). rodas5p_inner_forcing_target returned Err when the
roundoff floor 64 eps * rhs_wrms exceeded the 0.1 / ||b||_1 allocation,
i.e. whenever rhs_wrms > 1.4e12, and so aborted a stiff step at stage 0
before any GMRES iteration. It now returns the same floor-limited eta and
tau with floor_active = true, and the embedded error estimate judges the
step. Targets below the old abort condition are bit-identical.

Step C (F-008). The first stage-solve pass keeps the h-independent
allocation. Its embedded estimate err then bounds every stage budget by
0.1 / ||b||_1 * min(1, err)^(6/5) (exponent (p+1)/(q+1) for p = 5,
q = 4), never below 64 eps * max(1, flow_wrms, rhs_wrms). When a stage
residual exceeds that bound, all stages are solved again, warm-started
from the previous pass; at most two refinements run and all work is
charged. At a fixed tolerance the admitted residual now shrinks like
h^6 instead of staying at about 0.1 tolerance units. The public API of
sequential_matrix_free_step_with_inner_forcing is unchanged, so the
adaptive driver, dense output v2 and the regime atlas all use the rule.

StageInnerForcingReport gains floor_active and refinement_pass.
rodas5p_inner_forcing_error_limit and RODAS5P_INNER_FORCING_ERROR_EXPONENT
are exported.

- a1_committed_trace_regression: new baseline digest 8c61f4b0...b062b;
  the v2 digest 1df89540...9b61 stays as a record.
- frozen_full_e_shadow_contracts: first target R-JF JVP vectors

fix: stop Arnoldi only on an exactly zero residual; finite phi normalizer (VIG-A02, VIG-A06)

VIG-A02: krylov_phi_action, krylov_exponential_once and the fused prefix
session stopped the basis when h_{m+1,m} <= 1e3 eps max(1, |h_{i,m}|).
A nonzero residual below that test can come back with a large gain
(A = [[-2, 2^46], [2^-46, -2]], v = e1: leak 2^-46, gain 2^46), and the
first-term residual estimate then hid a true error of 7.35e-2. Only an
exactly zero residual now ends the basis; a small nonzero one is
normalised and extends it, and the ordinary checkpoints decide. On the
2x2 case both paths reach the full space: true error 4.08e-4, within
the conditioning allowance eps ||A||_1 ||exact|| = 3.26e-3.

VIG-A06: dense_phi_action built its normalizer as 2^ceil(log2 max|v|),
which is 2^1024 = inf for v = 1e308. The exponent is clamped to
[-1022, 1023] and the power of two is built from its bits.

Test corrections relative to the RED commit: the legacy full-space run
ends with an exactly zero residual, so happy_breakdown is true there
(assertion removed); phi_1(0) MIN_POSITIVE is one subnormal ulp off
because the Pade column is 1 ulp below 0.5, so the subnormal/power-of-two
test is an allowance of 4 eps |v| + 2^-1074, not bitwise.

Not fixed: at an ordinary checkpoint the residual term is still an
estimate. With fused minimum_dimension = 1, or the prefix session, the
same 2x2 case converges at dimension 1 with error 7.35e-2, before and
after this change.
